name: hopfield_network
evidence: memories are attractors of a weighted energy (cite:hopfield-1982); no bijection of a finite box is a strict contraction (lean:thm_ms_reversible_no_global_contraction), so a closed reversible mesh has no attractors, and the repo finds recall on a dissipative layer and failure on the bare reversible rule (E-MMR-0007); it needs stored weights and an outward sink, which M7 tests

name: sparse_distributed_memory
evidence: retrieval by Hamming proximity to randomly placed hard locations with counters (cite:kanerva-1988); the random locations become a structured address set, the counters are stored per location, and writing accumulates and erases; a laid-out content-addressable memory recalls exactly on the {3,4,3,4} bulk (E-MMR-0005)

name: hyperdimensional_computing
evidence: binding, bundling and permutation on long vectors, which may be ternary (cite:kanerva-2009); a hypervector is a laid-out block of cells, binding by elementwise product is invertible but bundling by majority erases, and the random base vectors become structured ones

name: content_addressable_memory
evidence: a parallel match of a key against every stored word (cite:pagiamtzis-2006); the repo's laid-out memory recalls every stored word exactly on the {3,4,3,4} bulk and on every buildable hyperbolic tessellation (E-MMR-0005; E-MMR-0016), with the key fed from outside

name: associative_processors
evidence: bit-serial word-parallel processing over a content-addressable store (cite:foster-1976); the max, min and next-value primitives run on the bulk at constant pass cost (E-MMR-0010; E-MMR-0011) but are laid out and erase their tag bits, so a history or sink is needed

name: bidirectional_associative_memory
evidence: two layers settle into a resonant pair through a correlation matrix (cite:kosko-1988); like row 56 the settling is a contraction, which a closed reversible box cannot do (lean:thm_ms_reversible_no_global_contraction; E-MMR-0007), and the matrix is stored per link

name: modern_hopfield_networks
evidence: higher-order energies store far more patterns than pairwise ones (cite:krotov-2016), and the repo measures the gain against the classical net (E-MMR-0004); the stored patterns are weights and retrieval is a contraction, so the same two ingredients as row 56 are needed (lean:thm_ms_reversible_no_global_contraction)

name: vector_symbolic_architectures
evidence: VSAs compose structure from binding, superposition and permutation (cite:gayler-2003); with ternary components each operation is a cellwise rule on a laid-out block, superposition by majority erases, and random atoms become structured ones as in row 58

name: holographic_reduced_representations
evidence: real-valued vectors bound by circular convolution (cite:plate-1995) contradict base:discrete_state; the discrete binding of row 58 is the analogue the mesh can carry

name: semantic_networks
evidence: concepts as nodes and labeled relations as links, queried by traversal (cite:quillian-1968); the mesh's links are fixed, so an arbitrary concept graph is laid out on it, and a content-cued walk from memory to memory already runs on the bulk (E-MMR-0003)

name: spreading_activation_networks
evidence: activation spreads from cued nodes and decays (cite:collins-1975); the spreading is the bulk query wave and runs logarithmically on hyperbolic geometry (E-MMR-0015), but the concept graph is laid out and decay erases, so a sink is needed

name: adaptive_resonance_theory
evidence: ART1 matches input against learned binary templates and commits a new category when the match fails (cite:carpenter-1987); the templates are stored weights rewritten by learning, and resetting a category erases

name: attention_based_computing
evidence: retrieval weighted by query-key similarity (cite:vaswani-2017); the repo shows the reversible rule is already a sparse one-hot local-attention update (E-CMP-0014), but learned projections are stored weights and the softmax weights are real, read only as an averaged description

name: tensor_product_representations
evidence: roles and fillers bound by outer products and summed (cite:smolensky-1990); with ternary roles and fillers each product is a ternary cell value, but the block grows with the depth of the bound structure and the sum leaves the three tones, so it is carried in laid-out blocks and superposition erases

name: heteroassociative_memory
evidence: a correlation matrix maps one pattern space to another (cite:kohonen-1972); the matrix is stored per link and the clean-up of a noisy cue is a contraction, which the closed reversible box cannot make (lean:thm_ms_reversible_no_global_contraction)

name: spiking_neural_networks
evidence: timed spikes carry the computation and spiking nets are at least as powerful as threshold nets (cite:maass-1997); a spike is a moving excitation the mesh carries, but synaptic weights are stored per link and the leak and reset erase

name: reservoir_computing
evidence: a fixed recurrent system transforms an input stream and only a readout is trained (cite:jaeger-2001; cite:maass-2002), so one fixed rule on the mesh is a candidate reservoir; the fading memory it needs cannot hold in a closed reversible box (lean:thm_ms_reversible_no_global_contraction; E-CMP-0018), only in the open ball with its outward sink; M4 found the open window forgets what moves (no moving lone excitation returns within 512 rounds on any open tiling, while 227 of 326 return behind a wall and 157 of 204 on quotients) but forgets nothing that stays in place (E-CMP-0051); the readout and the input stream are not tested

name: oscillatory_neural_networks
evidence: information in phase and synchrony of coupled oscillators (cite:hoppensteadt-1999); every orbit of a reversible rule on a closed quotient is periodic and the vacuum already keeps a Z3 clock (E-FND-0084), but phase locking is a contraction (lean:thm_ms_reversible_no_global_contraction) and the couplings are stored per link

name: boltzmann_machines
evidence: stochastic unit updates at a temperature (cite:ackley-1985) contradict base:deterministic; a deterministic chaotic stand-in would be emerges_with_structure (deterministic_surrogate), and deterministic reversible dynamics already reproduce a heatbath elsewhere (E-FRC-0092; E-FRC-0102), which M2-B tests for the spin-1 rules

name: perceptrons
evidence: a weighted sum and a threshold (cite:rosenblatt-1958); ternary weights and inputs keep it discrete, but the weights are stored per cell and the threshold is many-to-one, so the erased inputs go to garbage (cite:bennett-1973)

name: feedforward_neural_networks
evidence: layers of weighted threshold units, which stay accurate with ternary weights (cite:li-2016); on the mesh the layers are laid out, the weights stored and the many-to-one units keep a history, as in row 75

name: recurrent_neural_networks
evidence: rational-weight recurrent nets are Turing-universal (cite:siegelmann-1995), but by unbounded precision; with discrete states a recurrent net is a finite automaton (row 15) or, with laid-out unbounded memory, reached through the row 1 simulation (cite:margolus-1984; cite:bennett-1973)

name: graph_neural_networks
evidence: message passing with one shared update per node (cite:gilmer-2017), bounded in power by the Weisfeiler-Lehman test (cite:xu-2019); a shared update is one fixed local rule, which the mesh is, so what it lacks is a rule chosen by training and aggregation that does not erase

name: echo_state_networks
evidence: a fixed random recurrent reservoir with a trained linear readout (cite:jaeger-2001); the echo state property is fading memory, which no closed reversible box has (lean:thm_ms_reversible_no_global_contraction), so the open ball with its sink stands in, and the random reservoir becomes the fixed rule; M4 shows that fading for moving excitations only (E-CMP-0051), with no trained readout tested

name: liquid_state_machines
evidence: a spiking medium with fading memory and a trained readout (cite:maass-2002); the medium can be the mesh itself, with the same fading-memory condition as row 79 (lean:thm_ms_reversible_no_global_contraction), which M4 finds for moving excitations in the open window only (E-CMP-0051)

name: self_organizing_maps
evidence: units on a grid pull their weight vectors toward inputs and drag their neighbors (cite:kohonen-1982); the grid can be the mesh, including a hyperbolic one (cite:ritter-1999), but the weight vectors are stored per cell and learning overwrites

name: predictive_coding_networks
evidence: layers minimize local prediction errors (cite:rao-1999); minimization is a contraction, impossible in a closed reversible box (lean:thm_ms_reversible_no_global_contraction), and the generative weights are stored, so it needs both, and a self-kept boundary is the M9 form of it

name: active_inference_models
evidence: perception and action minimize free energy over probabilistic beliefs (cite:friston-2010); real-valued beliefs are not at the base, and whether a structure that keeps its own boundary in the open ball acts on its surroundings in this way is the M9 question, open

name: cellular_neural_networks
evidence: a space-invariant template coupling each cell to its neighbors (cite:chua-1988) is one fixed local rule; the discrete-time version with saturated outputs (cite:harrer-1992) is a cellular automaton, so the mesh carries it as row 30 with the saturation's erasure kept

name: memristive_computing
evidence: a device whose conductance depends on its history (cite:chua-1971; cite:strukov-2008); the analog device is not base, but a coupling that remembers is state kept beside each link, the per-link store that the second-order rules of M3-B carry

name: dendritic_computing
evidence: a neuron's branches integrate nonlinearly, a tree of subunits (cite:london-2005); hyperbolic tilings carry spanning trees (cite:margenstern-2008), so the tree is a laid-out subtree with stored weights and many-to-one subunits

name: pulse_coupled_neural_networks
evidence: identical pulse-coupled oscillators synchronize (cite:mirollo-1990) and image networks use one fixed coupling everywhere (cite:eckhorn-1990), so the rule is one fixed local rule, but synchronization is a contraction a closed reversible box cannot make (lean:thm_ms_reversible_no_global_contraction)

name: energy_based_models
evidence: inference by minimizing a learned energy or sampling from it (cite:lecun-2006); a reversible Z3 automaton conserves its energy exactly and samples the canonical ensemble with no random number (E-FRC-0099), so sampling has a deterministic stand-in, while minimizing needs a sink and the energy needs stored weights

name: physical_reservoir_computing
evidence: a physical medium's own dynamics serve as the reservoir (cite:tanaka-2019); the mesh is such a medium, so only the readout and the input are added, with the fading-memory condition of row 79 (E-CMP-0051)

name: petri_nets
evidence: tokens move between places when transitions fire (cite:petri-1962) and plain nets have decidable reachability (cite:mayr-1981); a charge-conserving collision is a firing (E-FND-0013), the net's places are laid out, and the free choice of which transition fires becomes a fixed schedule

name: actor_model
evidence: actors send messages, make actors and change behavior (cite:hewitt-1973); creating actors and passing addresses rewires the system, which the fixed mesh does only by encoding it in state and simulating it (cite:margolus-1984; cite:bennett-1973)

name: dataflow_computing
evidence: an operation fires when its operands arrive (cite:dennis-1975), which is collision-based logic: a gate acts where signals meet (cite:margolus-1984; E-CMP-0006); the graph is laid out and the matching schedule replaces firing on arrival

name: pi_calculus
evidence: processes pass channel names and so change who talks to whom (cite:milner-1992); the mesh's links never change, so the connectivity is encoded in state and run by the row 1 simulation (cite:margolus-1984; cite:bennett-1973)

name: communicating_sequential_processes
evidence: processes meet in synchronized rendezvous (cite:hoare-1978); a pair rule on a matched edge is a rendezvous of two cells and the schedule chooses who meets (decision 002), but the sequential processes themselves are laid out and simulated (cite:margolus-1984; cite:bennett-1973)

name: calculus_of_communicating_systems
evidence: processes synchronize on complementary actions (cite:milner-1980); as in row 94 the handshake is a matched pair, and the nondeterministic choice is replaced by a fixed schedule with the processes simulated (cite:margolus-1984; cite:bennett-1973)

name: ambient_calculus
evidence: nested boundaries move in and out of each other and dissolve (cite:cardelli-1998); the mesh has no nesting at the base, so the tree of ambients is encoded in state and simulated (cite:margolus-1984; cite:bennett-1973); boundaries a fixed rule keeps by itself are M9

name: bigraphical_reactive_systems
evidence: a place graph of nesting and a link graph of connections rewritten together (cite:milner-2009); both rewrite structure the mesh holds fixed, so they are encoded in state and simulated (cite:margolus-1984; cite:bennett-1973), with native nesting the question of M9

name: kahn_process_networks
evidence: deterministic processes joined by unbounded FIFO channels compute a fixed point that does not depend on timing (cite:kahn-1974), which suits the deterministic base; channels are laid-out wires carrying particle streams (cite:margolus-1984; E-CMP-0006) and the processes keep a history

name: tuple_space_computing
evidence: processes coordinate through a shared space read by pattern (cite:gelernter-1985); a laid-out content-addressable store recalls by pattern on the bulk (E-MMR-0005), but removing a tuple erases and a shared space costs routing time on a local mesh

name: bulk_synchronous_parallel
evidence: supersteps of local work, communication and a barrier (cite:valiant-1990); the mesh is already lockstep, so a superstep is a run of schedule periods, and the processors' programs are laid out and simulated (cite:margolus-1984; cite:bennett-1973)

name: parallel_random_access_machines
evidence: many processors reading and writing a shared memory in unit time (cite:fortune-1978); unit-time global access breaks the finite light cone (E-RLT-0015), so access becomes routing whose distance is logarithmic on the hyperbolic mesh (E-CMP-0004), reached through the row 9 simulation (cite:margolus-1984; cite:bennett-1973)

name: systolic_arrays
evidence: identical cells pass data rhythmically to neighbors (cite:kung-1982), which is the shape of a lockstep local rule; the data is pumped in from outside and the multiply-accumulate step overwrites, so a history is kept

name: population_protocols
evidence: finite-state agents update in pairs under a fair random scheduler (cite:angluin-2006) and compute exactly the semilinear predicates (cite:angluin-2007); a pair rule on a matched edge is such an interaction, so only the random scheduler is replaced by the fixed matching schedule of decision 002, on a graph instead of well-mixed

name: gossip_computing
evidence: random pairwise exchanges spread and average values (cite:demers-1987; cite:boyd-2006); a matched-edge exchange is a deterministic gossip round, but averaging to consensus is a contraction a closed reversible box cannot make (lean:thm_ms_reversible_no_global_contraction)

name: swarm_computing
evidence: many simple agents act on local cues to produce collective behavior (cite:bonabeau-1999); agents are particles the mesh would carry, their random moves become deterministic ones, and their behaviors are laid out; whether native particles have that repertoire is M3

name: spatial_computing
evidence: computation organized by the space it runs in (cite:beal-2012) is what a local rule on a tiling is, and the repo's knit runs as a cellular automaton bit for bit (E-CMP-0015); like row 30 a pair rule runs only over a matching schedule (decision 002)

name: aggregate_computing
evidence: programs act on whole fields across devices that only talk to neighbors (cite:beal-2015); a gradient field holds hop counts beyond three tones, so values sit in laid-out blocks, and building a field overwrites; reading a field as a description above the cells is M11

name: field_calculus
evidence: the core calculus of aggregate programs, functions from fields to fields (cite:viroli-2019); the same ingredients as row 107, with expressions laid out on the mesh and their results kept as a history

name: chemical_abstract_machine
evidence: concurrent reactions on a multiset of molecules inside membranes (cite:berry-1992); a conserving collision on the mesh is a reaction (E-FND-0013), the random choice of which molecules meet becomes a fixed schedule and deterministic mixing as in row 28, and the membranes are laid out

name: differential_analyzers
evidence: mechanical integration of real-valued quantities (cite:bush-1931) contradicts base:discrete_state; a differential equation read off ternary cells by averaging, as the knit's hydrodynamics are (E-FLD-0031), is the coarse-graining question of M11

name: dynamical_system_computing
evidence: computing by trajectories, bifurcations and attractors, universal already for low-dimensional maps (cite:moore-1990); the global map of a fixed rule is a discrete dynamical system whose orbits M1 measures, but attractors are contractions, which a closed reversible box forbids (lean:thm_ms_reversible_no_global_contraction), so they need an outward sink

name: ising_machines
evidence: hard problems become Ising ground states (cite:lucas-2014); the couplings are problem-specific weights per link, and a reversible spin automaton conserves its energy exactly (E-FRC-0099), so it samples instead of reaching a ground state unless energy leaves through a sink

name: coupled_oscillator_computing
evidence: solutions read from phase locking of coupled oscillators (cite:kuramoto-1984); discrete clocks exist on the mesh (E-FND-0084) and closed orbits are periodic, but locking is a contraction (lean:thm_ms_reversible_no_global_contraction) and problem couplings are stored per link

name: general_purpose_analog_computers
evidence: Shannon's model composes integrators over real-valued signals (cite:shannon-1941), which contradicts base:discrete_state; its Turing-computable content is reached through the row 1 simulation, never its real values

name: blum_shub_smale_machines
evidence: registers hold exact real numbers and compare them in one step (cite:blum-1989), which contradicts base:discrete_state; no finite ternary block holds an arbitrary real

name: hybrid_automata
evidence: discrete modes with real-valued flows inside each mode (cite:henzinger-1996); the flows contradict base:discrete_state, while the discrete mode switching alone is a finite automaton (row 15)

name: piecewise_affine_dynamical_systems
evidence: piecewise affine maps of the plane are already universal on rational points (cite:koiran-1994; cite:moore-1990); a rational point is a finite digit string, laid out in balanced ternary with carries and run by the row 1 simulation (cite:margolus-1984; cite:bennett-1973), while arbitrary real points are excluded

name: polynomial_ode_computing
evidence: polynomial ODEs compute exactly the computable functions (cite:bournez-2017) but over real-valued continuous trajectories, which contradict base:discrete_state; averaged ODE descriptions of discrete rules are M11

name: chaotic_computing
evidence: one chaotic element set by its starting state acts as different logic gates (cite:sinha-1998); deterministic chaos is native to the mixing class of M1 and a chaotic reversible collision exists in the repo (E-FLD-0001), but the starting states are laid out and the thresholded output erases

name: attractor_computing
evidence: answers as stable states the system falls into (cite:amit-1989); no bijection of a finite box is a strict contraction (lean:thm_ms_reversible_no_global_contraction) and recall fails on the bare reversible rule (E-MMR-0007), and M4 found no attractor in the open window either: no single-cell damage of a stored register heals in the open window, behind a wall or on a quotient (0 of 6760), because an error in a class that holds a trit in place stays in place and the sink removes only what moves (E-CMP-0051); so a restoring memory needs kept history or another added structure

name: simulated_annealing
evidence: random moves accepted with a falling temperature (cite:kirkpatrick-1983) contradict base:deterministic; a deterministic stand-in would be emerges_with_structure (deterministic_surrogate), as the reversible demon automaton reproduces a heatbath with no random number (E-FRC-0102), which M2-B tests

name: physical_annealing
evidence: a body relaxes toward low energy by giving heat to its surroundings; deterministic reversible dynamics thermalize with no random number (E-FRC-0092) and conserve energy exactly (E-FRC-0099), so the thermal noise has a deterministic stand-in and the cooling needs energy to leave through the open ball's sink

name: coherent_ising_machines
evidence: optical parametric oscillators with continuous amplitudes and quantum noise settle to Ising ground states (cite:inagaki-2016); continuous amplitudes contradict base:discrete_state, and the discrete version is row 112

name: reaction_diffusion_computing
evidence: chemical waves in a reacting medium compute by their collisions and patterns (cite:adamatzky-2005); concentrations are read as averages over ternary cells, an activator-inhibitor rule self-organizes stripes in the repo (E-SLF-0076), and the reaction erases, so the layout, a sink and an averaged readout are needed

name: excitable_media_computing
evidence: the Greenberg-Hastings medium has exactly three states, resting, excited and refractory (cite:greenberg-1978), and excitation fronts solve mazes and make gates (cite:steinbock-1995; cite:adamatzky-2002); the refractory-to-rest step is many-to-one, so the conserving mesh keeps a history, and the medium's obstacles are laid out

name: soliton_computing
evidence: the box-ball system is a reversible conserving soliton cellular automaton (cite:takahashi-1990) and soliton collisions can carry logic (cite:jakubowski-1998); a reversible box-ball rule on {3,4,3,4} keeps solitons through collisions (E-SLF-0127), while D4 gliders disperse head-on (E-SLF-0128); the soliton states are laid out and M3 tests M1 rules

name: wave_based_computing
evidence: computing by interference of waves; interference is exact at the base (E-FND-0107) and the knit's density waves superpose as a signed coarse amplitude (E-FLD-0014), so waves emerge, but sources, paths and the averaged intensity readout are added; second-order Z3 waves are M3-B

name: acoustic_computing
evidence: mechanical waves transformed by structure; the knit radiates sound at one speed (E-FLD-0013) and a gapless sound mode emerges from ternary tones (E-SLF-0045), so sound is native, while the scatterers are laid out and the pressure is an averaged reading

name: mechanical_computing
evidence: the billiard-ball model is mechanical computing by elastic collisions (cite:fredkin-1982) and its cellular form runs on the flat cusp (cite:margolus-1984; E-CMP-0006); the mirrors are laid out and the partition is a schedule, as in row 33

name: elastic_computing
evidence: mechanical metamaterials compute by deformation (cite:yasuda-2021); the mesh's geometry never deforms, so a strain field is an averaged reading of cell states, and elastic and sound modes of the knit are that reading (E-FLD-0013); the material's structure is laid out
